note: Verbatim pages from the two sources Phase 4 watches, gzipped because Kunena serves ~90 KB of markup for a page whose useful part is one span. The bytes are unmodified: nothing is trimmed, because the failure this guards against is a match found EARLIER in the page than the one we want, and a trimmed page cannot show that. Re-fetch from `url` if a parser stops reproducing these.

trent.why: One page serves every Trent auction in turn, so this fixture is whichever auction was live on the fetch date. 202643 is already recorded, which makes it the duplicate case as well: a scan against this page must propose nothing and say why.

trent2027.why: The SAME page a season later, kept beside the 2026 copy rather than replacing it. Trent rewrote the description for 2027 and it broke two captures at once: the sentence both the season regex and `orderStyle` key on ("This auction is for a 2026 Super Condensed $8k order") is gone, so against this page the shipped parser returned season null and orderStyle null. Season had a fallback and quietly took it, which is why nothing looked wrong — the fallback wanted "2026 SEASON" and the page now says "2027 Auction Season". `orderStyle` stays null here on purpose: it is a real loss, recorded rather than papered over, and the note it fed is replaced by the Trade 2 rule below. This is also the NEW-auction case the 2026 fixture cannot be, since Trent Auction 9 is not in auctionMetadata: auction 8 is the last recorded one, so a scan must PROPOSE from this page where it must stay silent on the other.
trent2027.tradeTwo: The page declares season 2027's second $8K order and which auctions get it, so the parse is checked against a rule the source states rather than against a guess: odd-numbered auctions are the "Trade 2" order. Auction 9 is odd, which is why the proposal leaves auctionStyle BLANK. The page hedges ("for at least the first 20 auctions") and so does the rule.

alesiev.why: The site went live carrying exactly these two auctions and nothing else, so this fixture is the whole listing rather than a sample of it. Neither auction is in auctionMetadata yet — this is the first source whose fixture CANNOT be checked against a recorded row, because there is no recorded row to check against. What replaces that is the badge vocabulary: 'Onyx' vs 'Non-Onyx' on two otherwise identical cards is the pair the parser has to tell apart, and the styles it produces are asserted to be values auctionMetadata already uses. UPDATE 2026-09-11: both auctions have since opened, been promoted and been published as season 2027 (20271 and 20272), so this fixture CAN now be reconciled against recorded rows and the test does — every recorded site Link must map back to its own auctionId. Two consequences for anyone changing that test: a scan against the LIVE sheet now correctly proposes NOTHING for these two cards, so every assertion about the PARSE replays against BEFORE_2027 (the corpus as this fixture found it) rather than against today; and season inference reads these cards as 2027 from the recorded span rather than assuming the newest season.
alesiev.note: `Aleisev's` is the site's own spelling in both titles and is NOT a parse error. The titles are copied verbatim, typo and all, because auctionName records what the auction was called.
